# Slice

Takes the elements of an array between two positions.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Slice(items, start, [finish])
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to take from, which is left unchanged. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `start` | number | The position of the first element to take, counted from 0. A whole number of 0 or more; a negative or fractional number, or null, is a runtime error. A start at or past the end gives the empty array. |
| `finish` | number, optional | The position just after the last element to take, so the element at finish is not taken. A whole number of 0 or more; a negative or fractional number is a runtime error. A finish past the end is read as the end, and a finish at or before start gives the empty array. When it is left out, or null, the elements are taken to the end of items. |

## Returns

Array. A new array holding the elements of items from start up to, but not including, finish, in order. Never null.

## Example

`Slice([10, 20, 30, 40], 1, 3)` returns `[20, 30]`.

`Slice([10, 20, 30, 40], 2)` returns `[30, 40]`.
